data.bottom_line: Hatcher Pass has entered a period of sunny, settled weather following last week's storm. Snowpack conditions are generally stable. You may still be able to find and trigger isolated pockets of lingering wind slabs or loose snow sluffs in steep and extreme terrain at upper elevations. Pay attention to signs of fresh wind loading like spindrifting, flagging at ridgetops, and smooth, firm or hollow-sounding slabs as you travel. Early-season hazards such as rocks, variable snow surfaces, and open water remain non-avalanche factors out there. Make a plan, practice safe travel protocols, and carry the proper equipment. Avalanche forecasts are published Friday thru Sunday or during periods of CONSIDERABLE or above Avalanche Hazard. ------------------------------------ SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENTS: State of the Snowpack: Thursday, December 3rd - 6PM @ Backcountry Bike and Ski Free Avalanche Rescue Workshop: Saturday, December 12th – 12PM-3PM @ Hatcher Pass – Fishhook (Marmot) Lot
